---
name: todo-due-date-rule
description: Todo app due date decision - local YYYY-MM-DD string, no UTC, overdue = strictly before today's local date
metadata:
  type: project
---

Decided 2026-09-13 by the user, to keep for the rest of the todo project: a todo's optional due date is stored as a plain `YYYY-MM-DD` string (or null) and treated as a LOCAL calendar date, never converted through UTC. "Overdue" means due date strictly before today's local calendar date, date-only; a todo due today is never overdue at any time of day.

**Why:** Explicit product decision, stated as binding for all later features.
**How to apply:** Never parse the string with `new Date(str)` (reads as UTC). Get today via local getters (`todayLocal()` in index.html) and compare strings. Any sorting, filtering, editing or reminders by due date must use the same rule. Open question: completed todos past due currently still count as overdue, per the literal rule. Related: [[todo-ordering-rule]].
---
name: todo-ordering-rule
description: Todo app ordering decision - completed below active, then priority high>med>low, then insertion order
metadata:
  type: project
---

Decided 2026-09-13 by the user, to keep for the rest of the todo project: completed todos always render below all active todos. Within each group, todos sort by priority, highest first (high, med, low). Within the same priority, todos stay in insertion order (oldest first). Un-completing a todo returns it to its priority/insertion position among active ones.

The priority rule was added later the same day. The user did not mention completion when adding it; I layered it under the completed-below-active rule rather than replacing it.

**Why:** Explicit product decisions, stated as binding for all later features.
**How to apply:** Any new feature (editing, clear completed, reordering, persistence changes) must preserve this. `todos` array is kept in insertion order; `ordered()` in index.html sorts at render time by (completed, priority rank, array index).

content.text:
Done. All three shortcuts work, and a 56-check browser test of every earlier feature passes. I haven't committed anything.

**Shortcuts**
- **Enter adds a todo:** this already worked through the form, so no change was needed. The test confirms it.
- **Escape cancels an edit:** this also already worked. The test confirms the change is thrown away, nothing is saved, and you can edit again afterwards.
- **`/` focuses search:** new. It does nothing while you're typing in any field (the todo input, date, priority, search, or the edit box) or when Ctrl, Cmd or Alt is held. It does work when focus is on a checkbox or button.

**Broken and fixed**
- **Phone layout:** on narrow screens, long todo text was squeezed into a column about one word wide, because the priority badge, due date and Delete button didn't shrink. On screens up to 480px wide, the text now gets its own line and the badge, date and Delete sit below it. The desktop layout is unchanged. I checked both in screenshots.

**Small safeguards added** (neither caused a problem in testing)
- In the edit box, pressing Enter to confirm a character in an Asian-language input method no longer saves the edit early.
- Double-clicking a row that was just redrawn can no longer leave the app stuck in edit mode.

**What the test covered:** adding, ordering by done/priority/insertion, the overdue rule for yesterday, today and tomorrow, marking done and undone, filters, search combined with filters, editing (Enter, Escape, clicking away, empty text), delete, bulk actions, saving across reloads, damaged saved data, no sideways scroll on a narrow screen, and no console errors. Run against the previous commit, only the two `/` checks fail, so the new code didn't break anything.

**Not changed:** completed todos that are past due still show as overdue. That's still the open question from the due-date rule.
